Tesla has issued an official statement to vehicle owners in South Korea regarding recent unauthorized devices that enable Full Self-Driving in the region.

Tesla reiterates that the use of such devices means you are entirely liable (in every respect) for any incident that occurs due to the device. This closely matches the expectations in regions where Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is available, such as North America and Australia.

The company has also mentioned that, in the region, the usage of these devices may violate local law and that usage is at your own risk.

As with other modifications and devices over the years (across all regions), Tesla has also noted that it reserves the right to refuse warranty repairs, regardless of whether these devices cause the damage.

These devices have been used in many other countries outside South Korea. However, we’ve not been made aware of any emails or other communications from the company at this time.

We applaud @Tesla's transparency about these issues and for giving developers a heads-up to prepare for this upcoming update.

As we stated throughout the thread, while these are technically labeled as security issues, no Tesla or third-party customer information is at risk.

The second issue allows for a thread actor to determine usage and performance (in other words, loosely how many vehicles you're processing on a node).

TeslaScope's Fleet Telemetry server infrastructure is configured not to use these parameters, so we're not impacted by this.

The first issue, which impacts all third-party services, allows a threat actor to impersonate other vehicles.

It's important to note that Fleet Telemetry is READ ONLY, so this can not result in any breach of vehicle information or user data.

Real-world impact is someone sending garbage or false data to our servers, which our systems already largely detect as outliers. We've not detected any instances of this security issue on our infrastructure.

Tesla has sent an email to all developers about two upcoming security fixes for Fleet Telemetry servers, which will be released on March 30th.

Both are low- and medium-severity; in particular, only one affects Teslascope, and we'll patch it immediately once available.
